summary.headline: Chambal Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA up 56% YoY to Rs 255 crore; FY26 PAT up 18% to Rs 1,950 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 14% YoY to about Rs 2,785 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 255 crore (9.16% margin) and PAT of Rs 145 crore (5.22% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 25% to Rs 20,794 crore, while EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 2,679 crore (12.88% margin) and PAT rose 18% to Rs 1,950 crore. Management attributed the Q4 urea EBITDA/ton jump mainly to product mix and ammonia sales, and said urea volumes were hit by a Q1 unscheduled shutdown and the Gadepan-1 turnaround running to mid-June. The TAN project (240,000 TPA) has entered commissioning, and the board recommended a final dividend of Rs 6 (Rs 11 total for FY26).

segments.name: Urea
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about Rs 2,432 crore (+8%), EBIT margin about 7.83%, volume 6.72 lakh MT vs 6.3 lakh MT. FY26 revenue Rs 12,566 crore (-5%), EBIT margin steady at 14.6%, volume 34.06 lakh MT (-2%).

segments.name: Complex fertilizers (DAP, TSP, NPK)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about Rs 323 crore (+94%), volume 0.65 lakh MT vs 0.38 lakh MT. FY26 revenue Rs 7,025 crore (+175%), volume 12.31 lakh MT vs 5.64 lakh MT, EBIT margin about 4%.

segments.name: CPC specialty nutrients and seeds
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue fell 21% YoY with EBIT margin described as healthy. FY26 revenue Rs 1,203 crore (+30% from Rs 926 crore), EBIT margin about 23.5%.

segments.name: Crop protection, chemicals and specialty nutrients (contribution)
segments.commentary: Contribution grew about 27% YoY in FY26; 17 new products launched in FY26 and 14 crop protection products plus one specialty nutrient planned for FY27.

segments.name: Biologicals
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 30% and revenues up 57% in FY26; UTTAM SUPERRHIZA and UTTAM PRANAAM covered almost 3 million acres since launch.

guidance_outlook: TAN: management expects about 9 months of production in FY27 at roughly 1.6-1.7 lakh MT, with budgeted realisation of about Rs 37,000-38,000/ton; margins said to potentially exceed budget.
Gas: current gas price cited at USD 18-18.5/MMBTU versus above USD 20 previously; no gas availability issues as of now.
Urea: FY27 volume expected to exceed FY26 (about 3.4 million MT), with 35 lakh MT described as touch-and-go.
IMACID JV: P2O5 capacity to rise from 5 lakh MT to 7 lakh MT in December 2026; sulphuric acid capacity expansion expected in FY27.
FY27 capex: routine capex Rs 170-180 crore (management also cited Rs 160-170 crore), plus balance TAN and urea spend of about Rs 500 crore combined.
G-3 urea plant expected to move to the new subsidy regime from 1 December 2026; government discussion ongoing.
capex_capacity: TAN project (240,000 MTPA, Casale technology) entered commissioning; weak nitric acid dry run has started, with AN Melt and HDAN commissioning underway; HDAN expected around end of month or slightly later.
Management said TAN run-rate target of 75-80% this year, per CEO's commitment to the business head.
Possible fourth urea plant (brownfield, about 1.3 million MT) estimated at Rs 9,500-10,000 crore; land and environmental clearance in hand; will proceed within 5-6 months of government policy.
Urea turnaround: Q1 FY26 unscheduled shutdown at one plant; Gadepan-1 shutdown (longer) running till about mid-June 2026.
Urea inventory at FY26 end about 1,18,000 MT.
demand_pricing: Management said industry-wide ammonia prices rose to USD 850-900/ton and sulphur to USD 900-950/ton in Q4 due to West Asia disruption.
NBS subsidy rates were raised about 10% by government; management said urea is cost-plus, so higher gas costs flow through subsidy except for working capital impact.
TAN market described as short with demand growth of about 6-7% per year (around 70,000 tons annually on 1.2 million tons demand); TAN prices reported up about 40%.
Phosphatic availability constrained by about 28-29 ships stuck near Hormuz; company stocks covered until about July-August.
Monsoon at 108% of LPA; Kharif acreage 112 million ha; pre-Kharif fertiliser inventory about 51% of seasonal requirement vs 33% normal.
Nutrien long-term agreement reportedly in place for nutrient-use-efficiency products; Indian market for such products cited at about USD 1 billion over 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Current gas cost for Q1 FY27 and whether receivables build-up will persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas around USD 18-18.5 plus, similar to prior guidance. Receivable build-up linked to escalation/de-escalation mechanism; company is seeking interim relief from government on higher gas costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did urea EBITDA per ton jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to product mix and ammonia sales at better margins, higher urea sales (30,000-40,000 tons higher) and a lighter turnaround load (one plant shut this year versus two last year).

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 TAN revenue and margins be strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Budget realisation about Rs 37,000-38,000/ton; management expects margins to exceed budget and no demand issues this year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the government support the sector if subsidy bills rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government is clearly committed to fertiliser support and will fund higher costs; not expected to repeat FY22-23 style receivable bloat.

qa_highlights.question: Net cash position at FY26 end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash and short-term borrowings were roughly balanced at year-end; the balance is fluctuating and expected to fall once Q1 subsidies are released.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for automotive-grade urea and phosphatic capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Automotive urea is technically possible from one or two streams but needs government approval and has no timeline. Phosphatic expansion is contingent on GST rework and pricing freedom; a possible overseas JV is being explored.

risks_watch: Receivables jumped to Rs 2,075 crore at FY26 end and short-term borrowings rose; watch the Q1 FY27 subsidy release and any escalation relief.
Gas supply and prices (USD 18-18.5 currently) and the risk of renewed West Asia disruption affecting ammonia, sulphur and LNG costs.
TAN commissioning timeline and ramp-up to 75-80% utilisation; Russian export curbs could affect TAN import availability.
Phosphatic supply constrained by shipping disruption; DAP pricing and GST structure remain open issues for new phosphatic capacity.
G-3 move to a new subsidy regime from 1 December 2026 with no clarity yet on profitability; government policy pending for new urea capex.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the TAN ramp-up, the fourth urea plant and demand, but noticeably cautious and deflecting on specifics (Ammonia volumes, G-3 economics, energy consumption and new-capex timing), citing government policy as the gating factor.
